title: How do we multiply 3874 by 11 in one line?
description: A number times eleven is written in one line by adding each digit to the one on its right and carrying. The result is checked by adding ten times the number to the number, and tried again on 5678. Keeko doubts that the extra one can be dropped.
teaching_notes: One idea: times eleven means ten times the number plus the number, so each digit is added to its neighbour with carries. Watch for students who drop the carry and write only the last digit of each sum.

source: Find 3874 × 11 in one line, and check with 5678 × 11.
video_script.why: The child can add a number to ten times itself. Here that sum is written as a quick one line rule.
video_script.substitution: Write the last digit, add each digit to the one on its right with carries, bring down the first digit, and check by adding.
video_script.anchor: three thousand eight hundred seventy four times eleven
video_script.wrong_answer: write one and drop the extra one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes only the last digit of each sum and drops the extra one every time, so the answer comes out as thirty one thousand five hundred fourteen. The check gives forty two thousand six hundred fourteen.
video_script.payoff_line: Times eleven adds each digit to its neighbour

final_answer.spoken: three thousand eight hundred seventy four times eleven is forty two thousand six hundred fourteen, and five thousand six hundred seventy eight times eleven is sixty two thousand four hundred fifty eight

never_show: a dropped carry marked as right
maths_rules: units 4; 7 + 4 = 11, write 1, carry 1; 8 + 7 + 1 = 16, write 6, carry 1; 3 + 8 + 1 = 12, write 2, carry 1; 3 + 1 = 4
dropping every carry in 3874 × 11 gives 31514, which is not 42614
video_script.design: One idea: times eleven is ten times the number plus the number, so each digit is added to its neighbour with carries. Wrong idea: the extra one in a sum of eleven can be dropped. The columns stay on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven plus four is eleven, so write one and drop the extra one.
